paragraphs: Brussels will ban all rental e-scooters from its streets in January 2027. The capital of Belgium is following other big European cities like Paris, Madrid, and Prague, which already stopped them.

Local leaders made this decision because accidents increased by 26% in one year, and hurt over 600 people. Doctors say that e-scooter accidents often cause bad head injuries. Also, people leave the scooters in bad places on the pavements. This blocks the way and makes walking dangerous for old people and people who cannot move easily. The government also said that dangerous criminal groups and drug sellers use these scooters to commit crimes.
Instead of e-scooters, Brussels will give more money to its bike-sharing system and put more regular and electric bicycles on the streets.

paragraphs: Brussels will completely ban shared e-scooters from its streets starting January 2027 due to growing safety concerns. The Belgian capital joins other major European cities like Paris, Madrid, and Prague that have already outlawed them.

The local government decided not to renew the licences of the operators, Bolt and Dott, after a 26% increase in accidents in 2025 left 666 people injured. Medical experts warn that e-scooter crashes often cause severe head and facial injuries. Additionally, poorly parked scooters frequently clutter pavements, obstruct public ways and create serious difficulties for the elderly and people with reduced mobility. Surprisingly, authorities also revealed a strong link to organized crime. They said drug traffickers used e-scooters in 25 shootings last year.
While rental e-scooters will disappear completely, Brussels plans to strengthen its transportation network by expanding the availability of shared bicycles and e-bikes instead.
